extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate accountants, securities lawyers, and advisors preparing SEC filings for business combinations and real estate acquisitions
extracted.subtask_short: SEC reporting for real estate acquisitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to apply SEC Regulation S-X (including Rule 3-14 and Rule 11-01) for acquisitions or dispositions that may be real estate operations or businesses, including significance tests, required financial statements, and pro forma disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring pro forma financial information (items 3–8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Securities being registered are to be offered to the security holders of a significant business to be acquired; proceeds will be applied to purchase a specific significant business; disposition of a significant portion of a business has occurred or is probable and is not fully reflected in the registrant’s financial statements; [Reserved]; pro forma financial information required by § 229.914 is required for roll-up transactions; registrant previously part of another entity and presentation is necessary to reflect operations as autonomous; consummation of other transactions has occurred or is probable for which disclosure of pro forma would be material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim list from S-X Rule 11-01(b) items (3)–(8). Use this when determining whether pro forma financial information must be included in a registration statement because the offering or transaction affects investor understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a business acquisition or disposition is 'significant' (20% substitution)
rubrics_metrics.description: A business acquisition or disposition will be considered significant if the acquisition meets the definition of a significant subsidiary in § 210.1-02(w)(1), substituting 20 percent for 10 percent each place it appears therein; or if the business is a real estate operation as defined in § 210.3-14(a)(2), the significant subsidiary investment test condition, substituting 20 percent for 10 percent, as modified by § 210.3-14(b)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the modified thresholds (20%) when applying S-X Rule 11-01 for registration statements, proxy statements, and Form 8-K significance determinations for business acquisitions or dispositions involving real estate operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources and timing of financial information for significance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination must be made using: the registrant's most recent annual consolidated financial statements required to be filed at or prior to the date of acquisition or disposition and the business's pre-acquisition/pre-disposition financial statements for the same fiscal year; however, determination may be made using financial statements described in § 210.3-05(e) or (f), pro forma amounts for the registrant per § 210.11-01(b)(3), or the registrant's annual consolidated financial statements included in a Form 10-K filed after the date of acquisition but before the Form 8-K would be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are three permissible bases (A/B/C) for the numerical tests—select the applicable source based on availability and filer status. Do not 'annualize' data when using pro forma amounts (see pro forma conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use and continuity requirement for pro forma amounts in significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma amounts for the registrant may be used for the periods specified if they only depict significant business acquisitions and dispositions consummated after the latest fiscal year-end and only include Transaction Accounting Adjustments, provided: (1) the registrant has filed audited financial statements for any such acquired business and the required pro forma financial information; and (2) if a registrant has used pro forma amounts to determine significance, it must continue to use pro forma amounts to determine significance of acquisitions and dispositions through the filing date of its next Form 10-K or Form 20-F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you begin using pro forma amounts to show significance, you must continue to use that basis until the next annual filing; the tests may not be made by annualizing interim data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous offering (blind pool) treatment for significance calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant conducts a continuous offering and applies Item 20.D. of Industry Guide 5, the income test does not apply. Determination must be made for the investment test (when based on total assets) and the asset test, using: (i) during the distribution period, total assets as of the date of acquisition or disposition plus proceeds expected to be raised in the registered offering over the next 12 months (excluding the acquired business for acquisitions); (ii) after the distribution period and until the next Form 10-K, total assets as of the date of acquisition (excluding the acquired business for acquisitions); (iii) after that next Form 10-K is filed, use normal guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For blind-pool offerings, include expected proceeds for the next 12 months when calculating asset-based significance during the distribution period; remember to exclude the acquired business from total assets for acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When pro forma effects need not be presented
rubrics_metrics.description: The pro forma effects of a business acquisition need not be presented pursuant to this section if separate financial statements of the acquired business are not included in the filing, except where the aggregate impact of businesses acquired or to be acquired is significant as determined by § 210.3-05(b)(2)(iv) or § 210.3-14(b)(2)(i)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if separate acquiree financial statements are omitted, pro forma may still be required if aggregate impact tests are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating whether an acquired entity is a 'business' for SEC reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The term business should be evaluated in light of facts and circumstances and whether there is sufficient continuity of the acquired entity's operations prior to and after the transactions so that disclosure of prior financial information is material to an understanding of future operations. A presumption exists that a separate entity, subsidiary, or division is a business; however, a lesser component may also constitute a business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the nature of the revenue-producing activity will remain generally the same, and whether attributes remain with the component after the transaction (physical facilities; employee base; market distribution system; sales force; customer base; operating rights; production techniques; trade names). Use these attributes to assess continuity and materiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'real estate operation' (S-X Rule 3-14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term real estate operation means a business (as set forth in § 210.11-01(d)) that generates substantially all of its revenues through the leasing of real property. The acquisition of a real estate operation encompasses acquisition of an interest accounted for under the equity method or, in lieu of the equity method, the fair value option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Substantially all’ is not a bright line; determination is fact- and circumstances-dependent. Real estate operations typically include commercial and apartment property leasing such as shopping centers and malls, but exclude businesses with revenues susceptible to short-term variations (e.g., hotels, nursing homes) unless leasing predominates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related real estate operations may be treated as a single acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisitions of a group of related real estate operations that are probable or have occurred subsequent to the latest fiscal year-end will be treated as a single acquisition. Required financial statements may be presented on a combined basis for periods they are under common control or management. Acquisitions are related if: (i) they are under common control or management; (ii) the acquisition of one real estate operation is conditional on acquisition of each other; or (iii) each acquisition is conditioned on a single common event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple related acquisitions occur, aggregate them for significance testing and consider combined presentation of historical financial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-14 does not apply to real estate operations totally held prior to transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not apply to a real estate operation that is totally held by the registrant prior to consummation of the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the registrant already wholly holds the real estate operation, S-X Rule 3-14 special presentation rules are not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective and amendments to S-X Rule 3-14
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-14's objective is to provide industry-specific disclosures necessary for investors while reducing the registrant's burden to provide excess financial information otherwise required by S-X Rule 3-05 that is not useful. In 2020, S-X Rule 3-14 was amended to eliminate differences from S-X Rule 3-05 where no unique industry considerations exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply S-X Rule 3-14 when unique real estate considerations justify abbreviated or different disclosures, but follow Rule 3-05 where industry-specific considerations do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples clarifying 'substantially all' revenue (shopping mall v. hotel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenario 1: Target Shopping Mall that generates substantially all revenue through leasing is a real estate operation subject to S-X Rule 3-14. Scenario 2: Target Hotel with revenues from rooms, F&B, and other services is not a real estate operation because principal sources are susceptible to variations due to market and managerial factors; S-X Rule 3-05 applies if the acquisition is significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples to test whether leasing truly dominates revenue; operational businesses with diverse, variable revenue streams are typically not real estate operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider for data center acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a data center acquisition is of a real estate operation depends on factors including: level/seniority of employees acquired; significance of revenue from leasing premises versus managed services; whether predominant value of acquired assets relates to long-lived real estate assets (buildings, power/cooling) versus shorter-term leased equipment (racks, servers); and whether valuation used a real estate model or a traditional business model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When significant non-leasing activities exist, registrants may consult SEC staff (CF-OCA) if they believe S-X Rule 3-14 abbreviated statements are appropriate despite non-leasing activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity-method investments and real estate operation treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial purchase of an investment accounted for under the equity method is considered the acquisition of a real estate operation if the underlying investee is (or holds) a real estate operation. The same is true when a registrant elects the fair value option in lieu of the equity method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the underlying investee does not constitute a real estate operation or business, the acquisition may nonetheless require Form 8-K disclosure if material to understanding future operations; that is a legal determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key similarities/differences between S-X Rule 3-14 and Rule 3-05 (significance, aggregation, presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Similarities: 20% individually significant threshold for consummated acquisitions on Form 8-K/registration/proxy statements; aggregation of individually insignificant consummated or probable acquisitions for registration statements and proxy statements; registrant required to provide pro forma information if aggregated unrelated acquisitions exceed 50%. Differences: S-X Rule 3-14 uses the investment test only for significance (with investment test numerator including investments and assumed secured debt), whereas S-X Rule 3-05 requires investment, income, and asset tests; periods required under 3-14 typically one year, vs sliding scale up to two years under 3-05; form/content differs (statement of revenue and expenses and supplemental disclosures under 3-14 vs full Reg S-X financial statements under 3-05); abbreviated financial statements allowed under 3-14 in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing between 3-14 and 3-05, determine whether industry-specific considerations warrant 3-14; apply the appropriate significance test and presentation requirements, and be mindful of aggregation and omission rules (e.g., omission after nine months in certain cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods and thresholds under S-X Rule 3-14 for filing acquired real estate operation financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the investment test condition (modified significant subsidiary test): (A) If condition does not exceed 20%, financial statements are not required. (B) If condition exceeds 20%, financial statements of the real estate operation for at least the most recent fiscal year and the most recent interim period must be filed. (C) If the aggregate impact of acquired or to-be-acquired real estate operations since the last audited registrant balance sheet exceeds 50%, the registrant must provide (1) pro forma financial information depicting the aggregate impact and (2) financial statements covering at least the most recent fiscal year and interim period for any acquired/to-be-acquired real estate operation for which financial statements are not yet required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 20% individual threshold and 50% aggregate threshold to determine whether and how many periods of acquiree financial statements and pro forma disclosures are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and calculation of 'investments in' the tested subsidiary for the investment test
rubrics_metrics.description: For acquisitions, 'investments in' is the consideration transferred, adjusted to exclude the registrant's and its other subsidiaries' proportionate interest in the carrying value of assets transferred that will remain with the combined entity after acquisition. It must include the fair value of contingent consideration if required to be recognized at fair value at the acquisition date under U.S. GAAP or IFRS; if recognition at fair value is not required, include all contingent consideration except that for which likelihood of payment is remote. For dispositions, 'investments in' is the fair value of the consideration, including contingent consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing the investment numerator for the investment test, carefully adjust for retained assets and include contingent consideration per recognition rules; use the 5-day average market value for aggregate worldwide market value when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation rules for significance testing (consummated and probable acquisitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must aggregate acquired or probable-to-be-acquired unrelated businesses and real estate operations when the aggregate impact exceeds thresholds (e.g., 50% for triggering disclosures). The categories to be combined include consummated but less than 20% significant acquisitions; acquisitions between 20% and 50% for which financial statements are not yet required because of the 75-day grace period; and probable acquisitions less than 50% significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple smaller acquisitions occur, aggregate them as required; if the aggregate impact triggers tests, apply the applicable disclosure and pro forma requirements.
